items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: I think Milt Hinton was on that and Buck Clayton and it was beautiful. We did two days.

ctx.x: Say something about that recording date, if you would.

Well, it was beautiful. Don Redman was so gifted, you know. Every note...I always said this about Don... all of his, if you're playin' harmony notes, all of his notes sounded good. And of course Una Mae was near the end of her career. I didn't know her but she had a tremendous sensitivity and she sounded good on the date and Hilton Jefferson and George Dorsey and, let's
see, who else was on that? I think Milt Hinton was on that and Buck Clayton and it was beautiful. We did two days. Yeah. It was just lovely.

items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: A lot of times Milton Hinton would be on the job... We'd all be -- with our tuxedos -- doing a job.

ctx.x: About a year and a half, yeah. And then, let's see what happened after that. Oh, I started working around different little jobs and then things went bad and I started doin' the

club dates and I had to learn the Jewish music and the Italian music and doin' some Polish jobs. And usually I was the only colored man in the band, becuase I could entertain, but I had to learn that music and that was quite an experience. A lot of times Milton Hinton would be on the job, a lot of times Zoot Sims or Buck Clayton. We'd all be -- with our tuxedos -- doing a job. A wedding or a Barmitzvah or whatever. And I did that for a long time. And then we started doin' the parks in the Youth Program and I got…
I'm not really sure if I know just what that is like...
